# Part 1 — Install three things {background-color="#ffffff"}

## Three things, in order {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.4em"}
Two of these you probably already have, or install in a couple of clicks.
The third is the one worth doing carefully.
:::

::::: {.mode-grid}

:::: {.mode-card .chatbot}
::: {.mode-icon}
🖥️
:::
::: {.mode-title}
A terminal
:::
::: {.mode-desc}
macOS: Terminal.app. Windows: PowerShell. Both come with your computer —
nothing to install.
:::
::: {.mode-badge}
Already installed
:::
::::

:::: {.mode-card .skills}
::: {.mode-icon}
📒
:::
::: {.mode-title}
Git
:::
::: {.mode-desc}
The ledger of tracked changes from Session 1. Install it now so Claude can
safely edit real files from day one.
:::
::: {.mode-badge}
5 minutes
:::
::::

:::: {.mode-card .agents}
::: {.mode-icon}
🤖
:::
::: {.mode-title}
Claude Code
:::
::: {.mode-desc}
The agent itself. Runs inside your terminal, not a separate app. Needs a

:::
::: {.mode-badge}
10 minutes
:::

:::::

::: {.callout-box .tip}
[Already have Git?]{.cb-label}
Type `git --version` in a terminal. A version number means you're done with
that one — skip ahead to Claude Code.
:::

::: {.notes}
Keep this brisk — the point is just "three things, here's the order." Most
people already have a terminal and often already have Git. Claude Code is
the one nobody has yet and the one worth walking through carefully.
:::

## Install Git {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.4em"}
Most Macs already have it. Windows almost never does.
:::

:::: {.split-grid}

::: {.sg-col}
::: {.sg-head}
macOS
:::
::: {.sg-body}
Type `git --version` in Terminal. If it's missing, macOS offers to install
the "command line developer tools" for you — click **Install** and wait a
minute.
:::
:::

::: {.sg-col .accent}
::: {.sg-head}
Windows
:::
::: {.sg-body}
Download the installer from
[git-scm.com/downloads/win](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
Run it and accept every default — the defaults are fine.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.callout-box .tip}
[Verify]{.cb-label}
Open a **new** terminal window and type `git --version` again. You should
see something like `git version 2.43.0` — the exact number doesn't matter.
:::

## Installing Claude Code {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.6em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.3em"}
Five steps, once. Work through them before the workshop so you arrive ready
to build.
:::

::: {.steps}

::: {.step}
::: {.step-num}
1
:::
::: {.step-body}
**Open a terminal.** macOS: press ⌘+Space, type "Terminal". Windows: open
the Start menu, type "PowerShell".
:::
:::

::: {.step}
::: {.step-num}
2
:::
::: {.step-body}
**Run the installer for your OS.**
macOS/Linux: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`
Windows: `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`
:::
:::

::: {.step}
::: {.step-num}
3
:::
::: {.step-body}
**Close that terminal and open a fresh one.** The installer taught your
computer where `claude` lives — only a newly opened terminal knows about it.
:::
:::

::: {.step}
::: {.step-num}
4
:::
::: {.step-body}
**Verify.** Type `claude --version`. Expect something like `2.1.x (Claude
Code)` — your number will differ.
:::
:::

::: {.step}
::: {.step-num}
5
:::
::: {.step-body}
**Log in.** Type `claude`. A browser window opens — sign in with the Claude
account tied to the plan you paid for. You only do this once.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.callout-box .warn}
[If step 4 says "command not found"]{.cb-label}
The fresh terminal from step 3 is what fixes it, nine times out of ten.
Still stuck? Close the terminal app entirely — not just the window — and
reopen it.
:::

::: {.notes}
This is the slide people actually need to read at home, not skim in the
room. Walk through it once at normal pace so the steps are on the record,
then move to verification.
:::

# Part 2 — Make sure it's ready {background-color="#ffffff"}

## Verify, end to end {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.3em"}
Three commands, three checkmarks. If all three run clean, you're done —
close the laptop and see you at Session 1.
:::

::: {.chat}
<span class="you">git --version</span>
<span class="cc">git version 2.43.0</span>
<span class="you">claude --version</span>
<span class="cc">2.1.4 (Claude Code)</span>
<span class="you">claude</span>
<span class="muted">Opens a browser → sign in → back in the terminal, ready.</span>
<span class="cc">You're ready for Session 1.</span>
:::

## No Claude Pro? Two alternatives {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.62em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.4em"}
Sessions are taught in Claude Code, so menus and commands won't line up
exactly — but the ideas transfer directly.
:::

::::: {.mode-grid}

:::: {.mode-card .chatbot}
::: {.mode-icon}
♊
:::
::: {.mode-title}
Gemini CLI
:::
::: {.mode-desc}
Google's coding agent for the terminal. Free with an ordinary Google
account — the closest free stand-in for Claude Code.
:::
::: {.mode-badge}
Free
:::
::::

:::: {.mode-card .skills}
::: {.mode-icon}
🌀
:::
::: {.mode-title}
Codex
:::
::: {.mode-desc}
OpenAI's coding agent for the terminal. A good fit if you already pay for
ChatGPT and would rather stay in that account.
:::
::: {.mode-badge}
Needs ChatGPT Plus
:::
::::

:::::

::: {.callout-box .tip}
[Curious which is "best"?]{.cb-label}
Wrong question for today. They overlap more than the marketing suggests, and
the best one is whichever you actually open. We use Claude Code here; nothing
stops you trying the others afterwards.
:::

## Where today's files come from {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {style="font-size:0.68em; color:#5a5e66; margin-bottom:0.5em"}
Nothing to clone or download before the workshop.
:::

::: {.callout-box .tip}
[Nothing to fetch yet]{.cb-label}
Each session's folder is a small `.zip` linked from the [training
site](index.qmd) — grab today's when we get there, or ask your trainer for
it directly. Bringing a laptop with Git and Claude Code installed is the
only homework.
:::

## If something doesn't work {background-color="#ffffff"}

::: {.callout-box .warn}
[Common snags]{.cb-label}
`command not found` after installing → the fresh terminal from step 3 is
almost always the fix. macOS asks to install "command line developer
tools" the first time you run `git` → click **Install**, wait a minute, try
again. Windows blocks the installer line → right-click PowerShell, choose
**Run as administrator**, try again. Browser doesn't open on login → copy
the URL Claude prints and paste it into any browser by hand.
:::

::: {.callout-box .tip}
[Still stuck?]{.cb-label}
Come a few minutes early to Session 1 and we'll sort it out together —
that's what the extra time is for.
:::
